title: Ready for dictation!
summary: Prepare Spanish dictations with rules and examples. Ask an adult to read the sentences aloud so you can practise writing too.
keyIdeas: Listen to the whole sentence before writing.
Start sentences with a capital letter and leave spaces between words. The sentences practised here end with a full stop.
After a dictation, reread slowly to check for missing letters or words.

basicKnowledge: D. Reflexión sobre la lengua y sus usos en el marco de propuestas la producción y comprensión de textos orales, escritos o multimodales

activities.prompt: What should you do first when your teacher starts a dictation? 👂
activities.explanation: First listen carefully to understand the whole sentence.
activities.hint: Use your ears before your pencil.
options: Write quickly without hearing the end
Talk to the person beside you

activities.prompt: When writing a sentence in a dictation, its first word starts with a capital letter.
activities.explanation: Sentences begin with a capital letter.

activities.prompt: Which punctuation mark is missing from the end of this Spanish sentence? ✏️
activities.explanation: This sentence states something and ends with a full stop. Questions and exclamations use different marks.
activities.sentence: Hugo juega en el patio con su pelota___

activities.prompt: Put the steps for this dictation in order.
activities.explanation: First listen, then write carefully, add the full stop and check your work.

activities.prompt: Sort these Spanish sentences by their word spacing.
activities.explanation: Leave a small space between words so they are easy to read.

activities.prompt: Omar checks his dictation: «la tortuga come lechuga.» What is the mistake? 🔍
activities.explanation: The first word needs a capital: La tortuga come lechuga.
activities.hint: Look at the sentence's first letter.
options: It needs a capital at the beginning
It needs a final full stop
All its words are joined together

activities.prompt: Match each part of the dictation to its rule.
activities.explanation: Capitals, spaces and final punctuation help make sentences clear.

pairs.left: The first letter of a sentence
The end of a sentence such as «Hugo juega.»

activities.prompt: The dictated Spanish word is «plátano». Choose the correctly spelt word with no missing letters.
activities.explanation: Plátano includes the letter l and an accent on its first a.
activities.sentence: Aisha come un rico ___ en la merienda.

activities.prompt: After finishing a dictation, rereading helps us check for missing letters.
activities.explanation: Rereading slowly helps us find and correct small mistakes.
